newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO to continue steel supplies to Kia Motors.
newsitem.headline: POSCO to continue steel supplies to Kia Motors.

text.p: South Korea said on Saturday the state-run Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) would continue steel supplies to Kia Motors.
The finance ministry said it would also encourage commercial banks and merchant banks to discount promissory notes issued by the Kia Group companies to their subcontractors.

"POSCO will continue steel supplies to Kia on the condition that Kia will pay its overdue payment to POSCO early in August," said a ministry official. "We are concerned about domino effects of the group's financial troubles. We will try to minimise damage to Kia's subcontractors," he said.
The Kia Group said on Friday POSCO had notified it would suspend steel supplies to Kia Motors without cash payment.
The notification came after Kia defaulted on Tuesday on promissory notes issued to POSCO for steel purchases in May.
POSCO sells about 300 tonnes of steel, or 15 billion won worth, each month to Kia Motors.
"Financial institutions and POSCO will be given some sort of incentives for their aid to Kia," the official said. But he did not elaborate.
On Wednesday the ministry said it would supply money flexibly to ease concerns within the financial markets.
